After completion of hydrostatic testing, the line shall be dewatered and dried until the dewpoint temperature of the line reaches a minimum of ‐40OF. Methods and limits for drying and cleaning shall be evaluated during detail design. 7 PIPE STRESS ANALYSIS 7.1 DESIGN LOADS Wheel loads will be evaluated for all road and Railroad crossings. They will also be evaluated at foreign line crossings where construction vehicles may traverse the foreign lines, i.e. to determine what protection measures may be needed. Pipe stress will be evaluated for thermal expansion for locations that may be bound and subject to such stresses. 7.2 LOAD COMBINATIONS Pipe stress will be evaluated for combinations of vehicular loads, overburden, and the potential range of internal pressure up to the design pressure. Page 15 of 20 Design Basis Memorandum 1997-000-PL-DBM-0001 Revision: 0 Pipeline Scope - FEED Date: April 28, 2023 7.3 BEND ANALYSIS Stress in potentially unsupported spans will be evaluated. 8 BUOYANCY CONTROL When designing buoyancy control, the Engineer shall consider the type of terrain, construction season and feasibility of site access, construction and equipment limitations, ease of handling during transport, and availability of materials for field fabrication of weights. Reference materials, including delineated wetlands from field environmental surveys and construction field assessments will be used to determine pipeline areas requiring buoyancy control measures. A minimum negative buoyancy design factor of 1.25 for fresh water shall be used for the pipeline when crossing saturated areas and flood plains. This will be accomplished by using concrete coated pipe or geotextile bag weights. 9 GEOTECHNICAL DESIGN A geotechnical investigation will be performed to establish subsurface soil properties, ground water elevations, and will include soil resistivity for Electrical Grounding calculations. Geotechnical investigation will also be required at all HDD crossing locations. 10 CIVIL DESIGN 10.1 STORM WATER MANAGEMENT A Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) using EPA guidelines under its National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES), shall be developed by the construction contractor. 10.2 SOIL EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL A Soil Erosion and Sediment Control Plan should be developed with proper consideration of construction ROW and TWS preparation, soil management (slopes), properly using of control devices, and construction ROW restoration and revegetation. Temporary slope breakers shall use silt fence, straw bales sandbags, etc. Permanent slope breakers shall use subsoil and stone. Trench breakers shall be sandbags, or foam, if approved by TRIMERIC OES. Revegetation shall be per environmental and landowner requirements. Fabric, mats, blankets, or straw bales shall be deployed to control erosion. Sediment control shall be via eels, rock check dams, filter socks, and silt fence. 10.3 ROW ACCESS ROADS Facility sites will require permanent access roads accessible to heavy equipment and truck traffic. Improvements should be made to allow all‐weather access. Recommendations from the stakeholders and from geotechnical investigation will be considered.
